stories.headline: Solar canopies boosted corn yields by almost 20% in a heatwave
stories.summary: In eastern France, where it topped 35°C for weeks, 5,500 solar panels raised 5 m over a maize field shaded the crop. Yields rose almost 20% versus open ground, while the panels made clean power.
stories.why: One field can now feed people and power homes, even as summers get hotter.

stories.headline: A rapid gene test gives kids' cancer results in 2–3 days
stories.summary: At Addenbrooke's Hospital, fast whole-genome tests on 54 children returned results in 2–3 days instead of 4–6 weeks. Some children avoided surgery, and a national NHS trial of 200 kids has begun.
stories.why: Faster answers mean gentler, better-targeted treatment for young patients.

stories.headline: A new egg-eating snake species was found in Ethiopia
stories.summary: Scientists described the white-throated egg-eater, an ink-black, harmless snake from Ethiopia's Harenna Forest that eats only bird eggs, cracking them with special bones in its throat.
stories.why: Even well-studied Africa still hides animals new to science.

stories.headline: Canadian students grow fresh salad indoors for school meals
stories.summary: In remote towns where lettuce arrives wilted, three schools use hydroponic towers. In Dinsmore, six towers gave 40 heads of lettuce in two months; in Eskasoni they feed 264+ students.
stories.why: Kids are solving food shortages in their own towns.

fun_fact: Female white-throated egg-eaters grow up to 92 cm long, males only up to 58 cm.
